turns.content: Can an intron ever excise itself from a primary messenger RNA without a spliceosome? Explain the RNA mechanism that would make this possible.
Can mature mRNAs contain different exon combinations derived from the same primary transcript? Identify the process and explain its consequence.

Now consider animal replication-dependent canonical histone transcripts. Describe their usual gene structure and mature 3-prime end, keeping intron content distinct from the way the RNA end is processed.
Which processing framework fits these canonical histone transcripts? Distinguish specialized 3-prime end formation from ordinary spliceosomal intron removal.
Evaluate the claim that some histone mRNAs end in a stem-loop instead of a poly(A) tail. Which histone transcript class supports that claim?

Evaluate the claim that introns are normally removed from animal canonical-histone primary transcripts in the nucleus. Use their usual gene organization and RNA processing to explain whether it fits the biology.
Of the claims about self-splicing, exon combinations, histone stem-loops, and histone intron removal, which is least accurate? State the claim in full.

How confidently can that comparison be made? Account for class-level qualifiers such as "many" and "generally", rather than treating them as an exhaustive survey of every animal lineage and histone locus.
Check the conclusion against the difference between histone 3-prime end formation and spliceosomal intron removal. Does it depend on confusing those two processes?
Give the least accurate claim, a concise mechanistic explanation, and an appropriately qualified confidence assessment.
